name: CA-16
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+25 partisan lean in the San Jose area
Liccardo's $2.2 million war chest versus Soulé's roughly $3,500 raised
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 97 percent
No public polls or outside spending signal any contest
model.rationale: A 25-point Democratic district, an incumbent with a thousand-to-one cash advantage, and market pricing near 97 percent all point the same direction, and Soulé's negligible fundraising leaves no visible path to competitiveness.
model.watch: A sudden influx of outside spending against Liccardo or polling showing Soulé within striking distance would warrant a second look.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
California's 16th District leans 25 points Democratic, and first-term incumbent Sam Liccardo enters the general election with a decisive financial edge: roughly $2.2 million on hand against about $3,500 for Republican Peter Soulé. No public polls track the race, and no outside money has materialized against the incumbent. Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 97 percent.

Liccardo won the seat in 2024 and represents a San Jose-area district where Republican candidates start far behind. Soulé's minimal fundraising leaves little capacity to introduce himself to voters or contest the incumbent's name recognition. The forecast expects a comfortable Democratic margin, with the main uncertainty coming from turnout variation in a low-profile contest rather than any demonstrated weakness by the incumbent.
